stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is relevant to text generation tasks within the AI ecosystem.
Categorizes the model using standard ML tags like 'transformers' and 'safetensors'.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: SpaceX announces plan to become a ‘major mobile carrier’
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: SpaceX is actively pursuing becoming a major US mobile carrier.
The company has acquired low-band spectrum licenses to facilitate this expansion.
The plan involves integrating the Starlink satellite constellation with mobile services.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline within the AI/ML ecosystem.
Key associated technologies include transformers, safetensors, and the Llama architecture.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting continuous context gathering and tool use for multi-step tasks.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speedup is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) utilizing the MLX framework.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when running coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for models.
The updated engine also contributes to higher quality outputs from the language models.

stories.title: Amazon's new Alexa Tablets drop the Fire branding but are more Android than ever
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Amazon is rebranding its new Alexa Tablets, dropping the 'Fire' branding.
The tablets are shifting towards a more Android-like experience, notably adopting Google Play.
This move signals a significant strategic pivot for Amazon's hardware ecosystem.

stories.title: Amazon builds 1,000th satellite, will launch space internet service by end of year
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Amazon is rapidly expanding its satellite constellation, reaching its 1,000th unit.
The company plans to launch its space internet service before the end of the current year.
The development highlights the intense, competitive nature of the global satellite internet industry.

stories.title: Nvidia's big bet on physical AI aims for safer robotaxis, humanoid robots
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Nvidia is heavily investing in a full-stack safety solution specifically for physical AI applications.
This technology is being adopted by robotics companies to enhance the safety of autonomous systems.
The focus areas include developing safer robotaxis and humanoid robots.

stories.title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models
stories.author: Yukang Chen
bullet_points: Introduces Long-WAM, a framework designed to scale the context window of World-Action Models for real-time robot control.
Addresses the critical trade-off between needing extensive visual history for accurate inference and the computational latency it introduces.
Demonstrates that the utility of long histories is significantly amplified when the underlying video foundation model is pretrained autoregressively (AR).

stories.title: RECAST: Learning to Compute the Right Context through Adaptive Evidence Routing
stories.author: Chuchu Fan
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation of conventional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) which relies on fixed, similarity-based retrieval.
The proposed method, RECAST, aims to improve context learning by implementing 'Adaptive Evidence Routing' for complex tasks.
RECAST tackles scenarios where necessary evidence must be derived through computation or aggregation across multiple heterogeneous sources, not just found in a single document.

stories.title: Rephrase Before You Act: Characterizing and Mitigating Language Sensitivity in Vision-Language-Action Models
stories.author: Yuchen Cui
bullet_points: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit high sensitivity to minor changes in instruction phrasing.
A small linguistic edit can drastically alter model performance, demonstrated by a 98% vs. 2% success rate on a stove operation.
The research characterizes this language sensitivity and proposes mitigation strategies, even when using rephrase augmentation.

stories.title: EngramEdit: Decoupled Knowledge Updates in LLMs through Conditional Memory
stories.author: Wenjie Li
bullet_points: Introduces EngramEdit, a method for decoupling factual knowledge updates from the core LLM computation.
Uses conditional memory architectures (like DeepSeek Engram) to expand LLM capacity using input n-grams for embedding lookups.
Offers a promising pathway to update LLM factual knowledge without retraining or modifying the fixed Transformer backbone.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models allow for fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers for yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary AI services and local, open-source LLMs.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings enhanced performance and broader GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to improve model support across diverse hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically benefiting Apple silicon users with wider model access.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Anthropic launches free AI security scans for open-source projects
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Anthropic has released OSS Scanner, a new service offering free security vulnerability scans for open-source projects.
The service utilizes Anthropic's advanced AI models to provide thorough and periodic security assessments for participating projects.
The offering aims to help open-source communities detect security issues earlier, though the full trade-off is not detailed in the snippet.

stories.title: AMD will bring FSR 4 to handhelds by the end of 2026
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: AMD plans to bring FSR 4, a framerate-enhancing technology, to handheld gaming devices.
The rollout is scheduled to happen by the end of 2026.
AMD has reserved the right to initially exclude older handhelds from receiving the update.

stories.title: Apple will reportedly debut its first touchscreen MacBook in three weeks
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly planning to debut a new MacBook Pro featuring a touchscreen.
The rumored launch date for the touchscreen MacBook and an updated iPad Mini is around October 27th.
This announcement follows a recent Apple event rumored to focus on smart home products.

stories.title: Microsoft’s new Windows Search is exactly what Windows 11 needs
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is overhauling the Windows Search feature, addressing long-standing user frustrations with Windows 11.
The new version is currently in testing and promises significant improvements in speed and capability.
The redesign aims to provide a more modern and efficient search experience for Windows 11 users.

stories.title: R.I.P. Margaret Hamilton, whose code saved the Apollo 11 Moon landing
stories.author: Jennifer Ouellette
bullet_points: The article commemorates Margaret Hamilton, a pivotal figure in computing history.
She is credited with developing the software that enabled the Apollo 11 Moon landing.
Hamilton was also instrumental in coining the term 'software engineering' and founded tech companies.

stories.title: Let's Encrypt cuts certificate lifetimes to 64 days starting February 2027
stories.author: Nick Indge
bullet_points: Let's Encrypt is reducing the lifespan of free SSL/TLS certificates.
The new certificate lifetime will be 64 days.
This change is scheduled to take effect in February 2027.

stories.title: Internal files add to evidence of an ExxonMobil climate deception campaign
stories.author: Nicholas Kusnetz, Inside Climate News
bullet_points: Internal ExxonMobil documents reveal long-standing internal climate change deliberations.
The news pertains to ongoing legal proceedings, adding new evidence to climate deception allegations.
The story highlights corporate knowledge regarding climate risks predating public acknowledgment.

stories.title: Never Look Back: Understanding Persistence in 3D Object Memory from Egocentric Videos
stories.author: Homanga Bharadhwaj
bullet_points: Introduces 'Ledger,' a novel system designed to create persistent 3D object memory from egocentric videos.
Aims to enable embodied assistants to recall object locations and histories, mimicking human memory capabilities.
The research focuses on understanding and modeling object persistence within complex, real-world daily activities.

stories.title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
stories.author: Micah Goldblum
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) used for fine-tuning large language models.
Augmenting RLVR with strong novelty incentives, intended to foster new reasoning strategies, has shown limited success and risks degrading model quality.
The core issue is that verifiable rewards only supervise a limited scope of the model's knowledge and behavior.

stories.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
stories.author: Mahmoud Assran
bullet_points: Introduces RoboJEPA, a new world model architecture based on JEPA for robotics.
Addresses the open problem of scaling latent world model capabilities with model size and data.
Trained on a large-scale dataset across 12 different robotic embodiments.

stories.title: SciExam for ENSO: Can AI Agents Build Climate Models?
stories.author: Shilong Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SciExam for ENSO, a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents in scientific research.
The benchmark challenges language models to build low-order stochastic climate models (specifically for ENSO) from real observational data.
Addresses the current limitation in AI research evaluation: assessing the validity of novel scientific models, not just matching known answers.

stories.title: Validity Without Ground Truth: What Stated-Preference Economics Offers the Evaluation of Language Models
stories.author: Catherine Louise Kling
bullet_points: The paper proposes applying Stated-Preference Economics to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) for subjective questions.
It addresses the challenge of evaluating LLM outputs where no objective 'ground truth' answer exists (e.g., valuing policies or weighing values).
It leverages established economic concepts like content, construct, and criterion validity to assess model responses.

stories.title: EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution
stories.author: Shilong Liu
bullet_points: Addresses the performance degradation of robot foundation models when environmental conditions or tasks change.
Introduces EmbodiedRSI, a method for active continual robot learning that guides self-evolution.
Aims to improve the efficiency of self-evolving agentic harnesses compared to current trial-and-error methods.

stories.title: Before They Can Solve: Predicting Post-Training Coding-Agent Performance from Base Models
stories.author: Jiantao Jiao
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of predicting which large language model (base checkpoint) is suitable for costly agentic post-training.
Traditional end-to-end pass@K tests are insufficient for agentic coding because they fail to account for critical issues like reliable tool invocation.
The paper suggests that current evaluation methods often collapse multi-step interactions into single prompts, masking underlying multi-step failure modes.

stories.title: A Society of Researchers: Designing Institutions for Populations of Autonomous Research Agents
stories.author: Tony Salomone
bullet_points: The paper addresses the emerging trend of deploying massive populations (thousands) of autonomous research agents sharing compute resources.
It argues that these agent populations will naturally develop their own organization, necessitating explicit design by researchers.
The authors propose a framework, a 'society of agents,' leveraging multi-agent systems tools to structure these large-scale research populations.

stories.title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
stories.author: Micah Goldblum
bullet_points: The paper addresses a challenge in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) applied to large language models.
A core problem identified is that adding strong novelty incentives to RLVR often degrades overall model quality.
The research focuses on decoupling the exploration process from the optimization process to improve RLVR effectiveness.

stories.title: Distilling Graph Geometry: Knowledge Gap from GNNs to MLPs
stories.author: Ahad N. Zehmakan
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of distilling knowledge from Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to simpler, graph-free Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) for efficient inference.
Current distillation methods fail to explicitly preserve the graph-induced geometry of the teacher model, leading to representational deficiencies in the student.
The authors identify two specific spectral failure modes (e.g., spectral underfit on sparse graphs) resulting from this omission.

stories.title: SciExam for ENSO: Can AI Agents Build Climate Models?
stories.author: Shilong Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SciExam for ENSO, a new benchmark testing AI agents' ability to build scientific models.
The benchmark challenges agents to create low-order stochastic models of ENSO (El Niño-Southern Oscillation) using real climate data.
It addresses the current limitation where AI research is often graded against known answers, lacking validation for novel scientific models.

stories.title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
stories.author: Micah Goldblum
bullet_points: The paper addresses challenges in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) applied to large language models.
A core problem identified is that adding strong novelty incentives during RLVR can degrade overall model quality.
The research suggests that verifiable rewards only supervise a limited scope of the model's knowledge and behavior.

stories.title: Rephrase Before You Act: Characterizing and Mitigating Language Sensitivity in Vision-Language-Action Models
stories.author: Yuchen Cui
bullet_points: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit high sensitivity to subtle changes in instruction phrasing.
Minor edits in language prompts can drastically alter the model's success rate in action execution (e.g., stove operation).
The research characterizes this language sensitivity and proposes mitigation strategies, even with rephrase augmentation.

stories.title: Your Prompt Should Do More: Effects of Retrieval Instructions in Embedding Models
stories.author: Filip Ginter
bullet_points: The paper investigates the performance of prompted embedding models, specifically when detailed retrieval instructions are provided.
Current embedding models are shown to struggle with reliably following complex retrieval instructions in practice.
The research analyzes the underlying mechanism by which these instructions influence the representations of retrieval queries in asymmetric retrieval tasks.

stories.title: Validity Without Ground Truth: What Stated-Preference Economics Offers the Evaluation of Language Models
stories.author: Catherine Louise Kling
bullet_points: Proposes applying Stated-Preference Economics (SPE) to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) where objective 'ground truth' is absent.
SPE offers a framework (content, construct, criterion validity, etc.) to judge subjective responses to complex LLM queries.
This bridges a gap in LLM evaluation for questions involving subjective value, policy worth, or competing ethical choices.

stories.title: PHRBench: A Behavioral Evaluation of Post-Hallucination Reasoning in LLMs
stories.author: Qiankun Li
bullet_points: Introduces PHRBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate Post-Hallucination Reasoning (PHR) in LLMs.
Addresses a gap in current research by focusing on how models resolve hallucinated premises at the response level, rather than just final outcomes.
Tests the behavioral aspects of PHR across four domains using 18 different large language models.

stories.title: RunningTab: Direct Workspace Interaction with Environment-Side Tabs
stories.author: Sung Ju Hwang
bullet_points: Introduces 'RunningTab,' a method for LLM agents to interact directly with a workspace's files.
Direct Workspace Interaction (DWI) allows agents to search and read files from a terminal without prior indexing.
The research highlights the need for mechanisms to track task requirements, read status, and progress during complex file interactions.

stories.title: CoTrace: Data Recipes for Training Terminal Agents with Harness-Model Co-Evolution
stories.author: Chien-Sheng Wu
bullet_points: Introduces 'CoTrace,' a method addressing the joint dependency of terminal-agent capability on model weights and the runtime harness.
Critiques existing co-evolution methods for treating training trajectories as undifferentiated replay buffers, ignoring harness context.
Proposes a systematic analysis of the interface between the model and the harness to improve training data utilization.

stories.title: Which Rollout Taught It That? BehaviorTrace and the Limits of Training-Data Attribution in Online RL
stories.author: Amit Nautiyal
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of attributing specific learned behaviors in Reinforcement Learning (RL) to their original training data rollouts.
Introduces 'BehaviorTrace,' an open evaluation harness designed to rigorously test and validate training-data attribution methods in online RL fine-tuning.
Uses a controlled 'planted behavior' setup to empirically investigate the limits and reliability of current attribution techniques in language models.

stories.title: Training Parallel Speculative Draft Models by Directly Minimizing Expected Decoding Rounds
stories.author: Changxiao Cai
bullet_points: The research addresses a training challenge in speculative decoding, a technique used to speed up LLM inference.
It focuses on training parallel and semi-autoregressive (semi-AR) draft models to improve drafting efficiency.
The core difficulty identified is that the draft distribution is dependent on the starting position of the decoding round.

stories.title: Navier-Stokes lost in translation: Why Lean verification of AI autoformalisation does not guarantee correct natural language proofs
stories.author: arxiv.org via Corbin
bullet_points: The article critiques the reliance on autoformalization to verify AI-generated mathematical proofs, such as those related to the Navier-Stokes equations.
The core issue is that translating natural language (NL) into a formal language (like Lean) does not guarantee the correctness of the final proof.
This highlights a critical limitation in current AI verification pipelines, suggesting that formal verification alone is insufficient if the initial translation is flawed.

stories.title: Human-in-the-Loop
stories.author: rfornal
bullet_points: The article discusses the concept of Agentic AI taking control of software development.
It raises a critical question regarding the necessity and safety of full automation in coding tasks.
The focus is on the 'Human-in-the-Loop' paradigm versus complete AI autonomy.

stories.title: AI Models Have a Spine Until You Give Them a Manager
stories.author: lewisawe
bullet_points: The article explores the concept of 'authority' within large AI models.
It suggests that frontier models, despite high capability, can be swayed by perceived seniority or authority.
The research benchmarks how models react to conflicting information when a 'manager' or senior reviewer intervenes.

stories.title: Google Requires Manual Fact-Checking for AI Content Before Website Publication
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: Google is updating its guidelines regarding the use of generative AI content on websites.
The new guidance mandates that AI-generated content requires manual fact-checking before publication.
This signals a growing emphasis by major tech players on content accuracy and responsibility in the age of AI.
